newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony denies pulling out of U.S. movie business.
newsitem.headline: Sony denies pulling out of U.S. movie business.

text.p: Sony Corp on Wednesday denied a media report that it had decided to pull out of the movie business by selling its U.S. unit Sony Pictures Entertainment.

Japan's Jiji news agency on Tuesday carried a report quoting U.S. media as saying Sony had decided to withdraw from the movie business, and had been looking for a possible buyer of Sony Pictures through a U.S. investment bank.

"We get that kind of rumour (on possible withdrawal from the U.S. movie business) almost once a month. It's only a rumour. We have not made any announcement and we don't have any such plans at present," said a company spokeswoman.
"We have been troubled so much by these repeated rumours," the spokeswoman said.
She said Sony president Nobuyuki Ide regards Sony Pictures as "an important asset".
In October, Sony named a new management team for its troubled Sony Pictures unit, the umbrella company for Columbia and Tri-Star Pictures.

Sony Pictures is now headed by John Calley, the former president of United Artists Pictures. Masayuki Nozoe, executive vice-president of Sony Corp of America, was named a vice-president of Sony Pictures, marking the first time a Japanese executive has taken an active role in Sony's studio operations.
The moves came after the company suffered a dismal summer at the box office that capped several years of poor performances.
The box office performances of its films "The Cable Guy", "The Fan" and "Multiplicity" this summer were disappointing, although video sales of "Jumanji" and "Sense and Sensibility" were strong.
